title: Multiplication and division facts
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Multiplication facts
sections.objective: Know the multiplication facts up to 12 × 12, and work out the ones you don't remember.
explain: 7 × 8 and 8 × 7 are the same fact: the order doesn't matter.
Every fraction problem uses these facts, so the goal is to know them without working them out. The check is 10 harder facts; you need 9 right.

visual.caption: 7 × 8 as a rectangle of 7 rows of 8. Move the split to break it into two facts you know.

sections.key: Know your facts to 12 × 12. If you forget one, split it into two facts you know.

worked.note: Don't remember it? Split the 8 into 5 + 3.

sections.title: Division facts
explain: Every division fact is a multiplication fact read backwards.
Picture it as sorting into equal groups.
sections.key: Division undoes multiplication: 56 ÷ 7 asks "7 times what makes 56?"

sections.title: Divide with a remainder
sections.objective: Divide when it doesn't come out even, and write what's left over.
explain: Write it as 9 R 2: tap R on the keypad, then type the remainder.
If your remainder is as big as the divisor, another whole group fits.

visual.caption: 47 ÷ 5: make groups of 5 and see what's left.

sections.key: Find the biggest group that fits. What's left over is the remainder, and it's always smaller than the number you divide by.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Multiplication facts, division facts and remainders, mixed together.
sections.key: Read the sign. Dividing: think of the multiplication fact; if it doesn't come out even, write the remainder.

hints.whole.mult-div.mult-facts: Split one number into parts you know. 7 × 8 = 7 × 5 + 7 × 3.
hints.whole.mult-div.div-facts: Think of it as multiplication: the number you divide by, times what, makes the big number?
hints.whole.mult-div.remainders: Find the biggest multiple of the number you divide by that fits. Then subtract to see what's left over.
hints.whole.mult-div: Read the sign first. For division, think of the multiplication fact.

misconceptionMessages.whole.neighbour-fact: Close: that's one group off. Check with a fact you know, like the 5s or the 10s, and count from there.
misconceptionMessages.whole.added-not-multiplied: That's what you get by adding. Multiplying means groups: 7 × 8 is 7 groups of 8.
misconceptionMessages.whole.remainder-too-big: The remainder is bigger than the number you're dividing by, so another whole group still fits.
misconceptionMessages.whole.remainder-dropped: It doesn't come out even. Tap R and write what's left over.
